fact: Access Now includes Annobon among places with indefinite internet and communications blackouts, documented through testimonies from 2024 to 2026.
Access Now attributes Annobon's internet and communications blackout, begun in July 2024 and still documented in its 2026-10-20 report, to Equatorial Guinea's government.
ISS Africa says Equatorial Guinea had a 14-month targeted internet shutdown on Annobon Island from August 2024.
EG Justice, IPI and Small Media Foundation say six activists were convicted over a conversation in a private WhatsApp group; the date is not given.
The same submission says at least 11 journalists were detained or dismissed for their work between 2019 and 2023.
The same submission says the government cut internet temporarily, in Annobon and nationally; the dates are not given.
The #KeepItOn coalition says mobile service and internet access in Annobon have been restricted since 20 July 2024, after the government's security forces responded to protests there with arrests.

The #KeepItOn coalition says 16 people who signed a letter to the government asking it to stop dynamite use were detained, and security forces held at least 33 people in connection with the Annobon protests.
Access Now says the Government of Equatorial Guinea continued to effectively cut the island of Annobon off from the rest of the world in 2025.

AP reports, from residents and rights groups, that internet access to Annobon island has been cut off since the residents' July 2024 complaint to the government and was still in effect at publication; the government did not respond and the exact mechanism is unclear.
AP reports, from residents and rights groups, that dozens of signatories of the July 2024 letter complaining to the government about quarry explosions were imprisoned for nearly a year.
